Entries.SourceTerm: 了即業障本來空，未了應須償宿債

Senses.PreferredTarget: If understood, karmic hindrance was empty from the start; if not, old debts must be repaid
AlternateTargets: With realization, karmic obstructions are originally empty; without it, former debts still come due
SearchAliases: karmic hindrance empty old debts repaid
Senses.Note: The pair holds two claims together: with understanding, karmic hindrance is empty from the start; without it, old debts still come due. Shiqi asks what to say after a debt has been repaid. Duanyu critiques a prior exchange that answers with “originally empty.” A recorded sermon makes monks examine the line beneath the robe. Pu’an uses it to address a student’s accumulated habits. Its force lies in the tension between insight and consequence.

Senses.Note: Damei tells his disciples that coming cannot be restrained and going cannot be pursued. He then hears a flying squirrel and gives a final instruction before dying. Miyun says the later critiques prove that someone understood him; Miaoyun faults an attachment to sound and form. Senses.Explanation: Spilled water is hard to gather back: once poured out, the prior condition cannot simply be restored. Masters deliver the phrase after a student proposes retreat, after words or actions have already occurred, and in verses on an overturned kettle or a death; it turns the ordinary irreversibility into a prompt verdict inside the encounter.
